title: Count Number of Bad Pairs
statement:
You get an integer array `nums` indexed from 0. Two indices `i < j` form a **bad pair** when the distance between the indices, `j - i`, differs from the change in value, `nums[j] - nums[i]`. Every other pair `i < j` (where the two are equal) is good.

Return how many bad pairs `nums` contains.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every pair is O(n²), too slow for 10^5 values. Rearrange the condition: `j - i == nums[j] - nums[i]` is the same as `nums[i] - i == nums[j] - j`. So a pair is good exactly when both indices share the same key `nums[x] - x`. Counting good pairs is easy with a hash map of keys, and every pair that is not good is bad.

## Approach

1. Keep a map `seen` from each key `nums[x] - x` to how many earlier indices had it, and a counter `bad`.
2. Walk `j` from left to right and compute `key = nums[j] - j`.
3. Of the `j` indices before `j`, `good` of them share the key; the other `j - good` form bad pairs with `j`, so add that to `bad`.
4. Record `j` in the map by increasing the count for `key`.
5. Return `bad`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [4,1,3,3]`. The keys are `4, 0, 1, 0`.
- `j = 0`: key 4, no earlier index, `bad = 0`.
- `j = 1`: key 0, `good = 0`, adds `1`, `bad = 1`.
- `j = 2`: key 1, `good = 0`, adds `2`, `bad = 3`.
- `j = 3`: key 0 was seen once (index 1), so `good = 1` and it adds `3 - 1 = 2`, `bad = 5`.

The answer is `5`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant-time map work per index.
- Space: O(n) for the map in the worst case, when every key is different.

## Pitfalls

- The answer can reach about n²/2 ≈ 5·10^9, which overflows a 32-bit integer; use a 64-bit counter in Java or C.
- Keep the key as `nums[x] - x` (or `x - nums[x]`) consistently; mixing the two signs breaks the matching.
- Add the bad pairs for `j` before recording `j` itself, or an index would pair with itself.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seen` | map from key `nums[x] - x` to how many earlier indices have it |
| `bad` | number of bad pairs found so far |
| `j` | the right index of the pairs being counted |
| `key` | `nums[j] - j`, equal for every index that forms a good pair with `j` |
| `good` | how many earlier indices form a good pair with `j` |

narration.2: The map counts how many indices so far have each value of nums[x] - x.
narration.4: Treat each index j as the right end of its pairs.
narration.5: Indices with the same nums[x] - x are exactly the good partners.
narration.6: Look up how many earlier indices share that key.
narration.7: All j earlier indices pair with j; the ones that do not share the key are bad.
narration.8: Record j so later indices can pair with it.
narration.10: Every pair has been classified; return the bad ones.
